battle.name: 捷波戰爭
battle.brief: 捷波戰爭是中文維基「戰爭列表」所列一九一九年的波蘭與捷克斯洛伐克武裝衝突，主要戰區位於西里西亞的捷波地區。參戰軍隊中的俄系步兵使用別丹步槍（Berdan rifle），此型號在一九一九年前已列裝，屬於前線步兵的單兵武器。

kit.name: 別丹步槍
kit.history: 別丹步槍是俄系軍隊使用的栓動步槍，列入步兵分隊的小武器序列，作為普通步槍手的單兵武器，並非騎兵或炮兵裝備。

countries: 1919年「捷波戰爭」所指的交戰國是捷克斯洛伐克與第二波蘭共和國；法國不是作戰方，而以巴黎大使會議軍事代表的身分促成停戰。捷克斯洛伐克一方由布拉格、摩拉維亞基地調來的軍團正規步兵、炮兵、工兵及地方駐軍構成；波蘭一方以波蘭軍團第一師為骨架，結合泰申西里西亞地方起義武裝、騎兵與後勤單位。主要縱隊沿奧匈帝國時期留下的鐵路、公路和車站網推進；本文只記1919年7月的第一次泰申衝突，不把1920年10月的第二次邊境戰鬥混入。
countriesEn: The belligerents in the 1919 Czechoslovak–Polish War were Czechoslovakia and the Second Polish Republic. France was not a combatant but helped bring about the armistice through its military representative to the Paris Conference of Ambassadors. The Czechoslovak field army drew on regular Legion infantry, artillery, engineers, and local garrisons dispatched from bases in Prague and Moravia. The Polish side used the 1st Division of the Polish Legions as its regular core, supported by Silesian insurgent units, cavalry, and logistics detachments. The principal columns advanced along the railway, road, and station network inherited from Austria-Hungary. This account covers only the first conflict over Cieszyn Silesia in July 1919 and does not mix in the second border clash of October 1920.
people: 波蘭方面的核心人物是瓦迪斯瓦夫·科爾凡蒂，他主持泰申西里西亞的波蘭軍事委員會，籌組地方武裝、安排起義行動，並接應進入戰區的正規軍。愛德華·雷茲-希米格維以波蘭軍團最高指揮官的身分率第一師參戰，負責建立軍團作戰指揮與補給環節。捷克斯洛伐克外交部長愛德華·貝內斯代表政府堅持對泰申西里西亞的領土要求；泰申西里西亞民族委員會主席雅恩·普魯西克則主張把爭議區分給兩個新國家。法國將軍路易-歐仁·福謝代表巴黎大使會議斡旋，並於米托主持停戰談判。科爾凡蒂代表政治組織，雷茲-希米格維代表軍事指揮，貝內斯與普魯西克代表捷克方面的政治立場，福謝則是兩國停止戰鬥的直接協商者。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Polish side was Władysław Korfanty, who chaired the Polish Military National Committee in Cieszyn Silesia, organized the local forces, coordinated the insurgent offensive, and prepared the arrival of regular troops. Edward Rydz-Śmigły, then the senior commander of the Polish Legions, brought the 1st Division into the theatre and established the Legions’ field command and supply system. Czechoslovak foreign minister Edvard Beneš represented the government’s territorial claim, while Jan Prusik, chairman of the National Council of Cieszyn Silesia, advocated dividing the disputed region between the two new states. French general Louis-Eugène Faucher represented the Paris Conference of Ambassadors, mediated between the two sides, and negotiated the armistice at Mýto. Korfanty embodied political organization, Rydz-Śmigły commanded the regular military effort, Beneš and Prusik articulated the Czechoslovak political position, and Faucher was the direct intermediary for ending the fighting.
kits: 捷克斯洛伐克軍的步槍以Škoda vz. 1895，亦即曼利徹M1895為主，使用8×50R毫米R子彈；同時仍可見奧匈軍留下的施泰爾M1888/90步槍。制式重機槍為水冷式Schwarzlose M1907/12，口徑8×43R；炮兵使用Škoda 75毫米L/11野戰炮及10.5厘米M.15輕型野戰榴彈炮，部分軍團仍穿改用捷國徽章的奧匈軍服及奧制鋼盔。波蘭軍以莫辛-納甘特M1891及M1907-30步槍為主，使用7.62×54R毫米R子彈，並收編相當數量的施泰爾M1888/90步槍與Schwarzlose M1907/12重機槍。炮兵包括75毫米wz. 1897、75毫米wz. 1905/13野戰炮和105毫米wz. 1913榴彈炮，地方起義武裝另有馬刀、騎兵裝具及由波蘭軍團分發的步兵裝備。雙方都靠馬車、載重汽車、鐵路列車和鐵路平板車運輸，野戰電話、傳令兵與自行車連結各連隊；彈藥依口徑分庫發放，因此後勤線長度、馬匹數量及火車班次，往往比射擊精度更直接影響持續作戰能力。
kitsEn: The principal Czechoslovak rifle was the Škoda vz. 1895, a Mannlicher M1895-pattern weapon chambered in 8×50R, although Austrian Steyr M1888/90 rifles captured from the former imperial arsenal also remained in use. The standard heavy machine gun was the water-cooled Schwarzlose M1907/12 in 8×43R. The artillery included the Škoda 75 mm L/11 field gun and 10.5 cm M.15 light field howitzer, and many Legion personnel still wore modified Austro-Hungarian uniforms and Austrian-pattern steel helmets. The Polish infantry relied chiefly on the Mosin-Nagant M1891 and M1907-30 rifles in 7.62×54R, supplemented by captured Steyr M1888/90 rifles and Schwarzlose M1907/12 machine guns. Polish artillery included the 75 mm wz. 1897, 75 mm wz. 1905/13 field guns, and the 105 mm wz. 1913 howitzer; the insurgent formations also received sabres, cavalry equipment, and infantry gear distributed by the Legions. Both sides moved men and ammunition by horse-drawn wagons, lorries, trains, and railway flatcars, while field telephones, mounted messengers, and bicycles linked individual companies. Ammunition was sorted by caliber before issue, making the length of the supply route, the number of available horses, and the timing of railway trains at least as important to sustained operations as gunnery accuracy.
tactics: 戰役前段是一場由外交判斷轉成軍事的占領競逐。6月18日，捷克斯洛伐克軍越過奧匈舊邊界，進入泰申西里西亞的大部分城鎮，先行控制博胡明鐵路樞紐，並在車站院落、橋頭和路堤附近建立互相支援的陣位。波方沒有立即形成一條完整而連續的戰線，地方起義隊伍分散攻擊較小的駐軍哨位與孤立車站，波蘭軍團第一師則集中兵力向主要道路和鐵路接近。7月25日發動的協同攻勢中，地方武裝先行切斷捷軍外圍聯繫，軍團步兵隨後沿博胡明與斯科措夫方向推進，至7月26日前後奪取博胡明、斯科措夫等關鍵站點，使捷方北側的調度與補給受到牽動。捷軍利用既有野戰陣位，以75毫米炮和105毫米榴彈炮封鎖道路，再由預備步兵逐點反攻；7月27日以後的戰鬥集中在車站、鐵路側壕與城鎮外緣，短距離槍火和逐點爭奪反覆拉鋸。雙方都需要重新鞏固鐵路、補充彈藥並調整部署，法國代表抵達前線促成雙方同意沿當時控制線停火。7月31日，在米托簽訂停戰協議，交火停止，爭議區被分成南北兩個控制帶，沒有任何一方能把全區一口氣據為己有。
tacticsEn: The opening phase was a contest between diplomatic decisions and military possession. On 18 June, Czechoslovak troops crossed the former Austro-Hungarian frontier, entered most of the towns in Cieszyn Silesia, seized the Bohumín railway junction, and established mutually supporting positions around station yards, bridges, and railway embankments. The Polish side initially lacked a single continuous front: local insurgent formations attacked isolated garrisons and small posts, while the 1st Division of the Polish Legions concentrated on the principal roads and railway approaches. During the coordinated offensive of 25 July, the insurgents disrupted the Czechoslovak perimeter before the Legion infantry advanced toward Bohumín and Skoczów. By about 26 July, key stations including Bohumín and Skoczów had fallen, complicating Czechoslovak movement and supply on the northern side. The Czechoslovaks used their prepared field positions, covering the roads with 75 mm guns and 105 mm howitzers, and counterattacked with reserve infantry. From 27 July, fighting concentrated around stations, railway ditches, and the outskirts of towns, producing repeated close-range exchanges and struggles for individual positions. Both sides had to repair railway links, replenish ammunition, and redeploy before further operations could continue. The arrival of the French representative helped induce both governments to accept a ceasefire along the existing lines of control. On 31 July, an armistice was signed at Mýto. The fighting stopped with the disputed region divided into northern and southern control zones; neither army had gained possession of the entire area.
data: 這場戰役通常稱為泰申西里西亞第一次衝突，也因1919年7月25日至31日連續七個日曆日而稱「七日戰爭」。主要戰場是泰申西里西亞及其鐵路網，尤其集中於博胡明樞紐、泰申方向線路及斯科措夫通往西部城鎮的支線。作戰單位規模介於團、旅與師級臨時指揮群之間；捷方以捷軍團正規部隊為主，波方則把波蘭軍團第一師、地方起義民兵、騎兵和後勤分散編入不同攻擊群。現存史料常把尚未抵達、正在換防或只短暫參戰的部隊一併計入，因此雙方兵力的公開總數無法可靠比較；傷亡紀錄同樣缺少雙方共同採用的統計基準，個別戰報又有缺頁、重複計算和把作戰與後方傷病混列的情形，因此不列任何未經核實的精確傷亡總數。可以確定的是，七日戰爭在主戰線尚未被任何一方突破的情況下，以停戰而非一方攻佔全區收場。
dataEn: This campaign is generally known as the first conflict over Cieszyn Silesia and, because it ran from 25 to 31 July 1919, as the Seven Days’ War. Its principal area was Cieszyn Silesia and its railway network, especially the Bohumín junction, the line toward Cieszyn, and the branch running west from Skoczów. The formations involved varied between regimental, brigade-sized, and temporary divisional command groups. The Czechoslovak force was built around regular Legion units, while the Polish side distributed the 1st Division of the Polish Legions, Silesian insurgent militia, cavalry, and logistics personnel among separate attacking groups. Surviving accounts often counted units that had not yet arrived, were changing positions, or took part only briefly, so published overall strength figures cannot be compared reliably. Casualty records also lack a common accounting basis; individual reports contain missing entries, duplicate names, and an unclear mixture of battle casualties and later sickness. For that reason, no unverified exact total is given here. What can be established is that the seven-day war ended in an armistice while neither side had broken through the main front or occupied the entire disputed territory.
cause: 戰爭源於奧匈帝國在1918年解體後，泰申西里西亞的歸屬沒有得到確定。1918年10月12日成立的泰申西里西亞民族委員會曾以整個區域為行政範圍，但捷克與波蘭的中央政府很快都把這片土地納入各自的國家計畫。波方重視泰申城及其通往波蘭的交通線，捷方則著重南部盆地、煤礦工業與連接摩拉維亞、斯洛伐克的鐵路。1919年春季的斯帕會議及巴黎大使會議提出切分爭議區的原則，卻沒有得到波蘭接受。6月18日以後，捷克斯洛伐克軍進入多數城鎮，以實際占領固定既成局勢；波蘭政府拒絕接受劃界結果，地方軍事委員會開始武裝準備，波蘭軍團第一師也進入戰區。由於車站、橋梁、煤礦和鐵路調度直接關係兩國在新邊界上的行政與軍事運作，邊界會議未能解決的問題很快轉化為正面軍事衝突。
causeEn: The war arose because the collapse of Austria-Hungary in 1918 left the status of Cieszyn Silesia unresolved. The National Council of Cieszyn Silesia, established on 12 October 1918, initially treated the whole region as an administrative unit, but the central governments in Prague and Warsaw soon incorporated it into their respective national plans. Poland emphasized Cieszyn and its transport links toward Polish territory, while Czechoslovakia focused on the southern basin, the coal industry, and the railways connecting the area with Moravia and Slovakia. The Spa meetings and the Paris Conference of Ambassadors proposed dividing the disputed region during the spring of 1919, but Poland did not accept that proposal. After Czechoslovak troops entered most of the towns on 18 June, military occupation began to establish the situation on the ground. The Polish government rejected the projected line, the local military committee began armed preparations, and the 1st Division of the Polish Legions entered the theatre. Because stations, bridges, mines, and railway movements directly affected the administrative and military operation of both new states, a boundary dispute that diplomatic conferences had not resolved rapidly became an armed conflict.
impact: 停戰線很快成為實際上的分界基礎。雙方在鐵路沿線保留機場、哨所與路障，原本可以連續運行的博胡明樞紐被分割成兩套調度系統，後續火車與補給車必須按新的邊境手續分線行駛。波蘭在軍事上未能取得泰申西里西亞多數城鎮，科爾凡蒂仍於8月14日在泰申體育場宣布成立泰申西里西亞自治邦，並建立一套與波蘭行政相連的機關；然而這一宣布沒有取得與實際控制相稱的國際承認。捷克斯洛伐克則保住了大部分南部工業與交通區，使波蘭的主張縮入北部較小區域。這次結果加深了兩國對邊界與軍團部署的戒心。停戰只處理前線，沒有解決根本爭議，雙方仍不接受大使會議的劃分方案，最終在1920年10月爆發第二次五日邊境衝突。
impactEn: The armistice line quickly became the practical basis for the frontier. Both sides retained emplacements, guard posts, and roadblocks along the railway, while the Bohumín junction was split into separate operating systems. Later trains and supply convoys had to be routed and processed according to the new border arrangements. Militarily, Poland had failed to secure most of the towns in Cieszyn Silesia, yet Korfanty proclaimed the State of Cieszyn Silesia at the Cieszyn stadium on 14 August and created administrative institutions connected with Poland. The proclamation did not, however, receive recognition commensurate with the territory actually controlled. Czechoslovakia retained the southern industrial and transport zone, reducing the Polish claim to a smaller northern area. The outcome deepened mutual suspicion over the frontier and the deployment of the Legions. The armistice settled the immediate front but not the underlying dispute: neither side accepted the proposed partition, and a second conflict, known as the Five-Day War, followed in October 1920.
result: 1919年戰役的直接結果是7月31日米托停戰，而不是任何一方取得泰申西里西亞全境。停戰時，捷克斯洛伐克控制南部較大的工業與鐵路區，波蘭則保住北部包括泰申城在內的一段；因此在戰術上是僵持，在戰略與外交上則是捷克斯洛伐克占優。巴黎大使會議於1920年8月28日正式劃界，把2,820.4平方公里判給捷克斯洛伐克，把包括泰申城在內的214.3平方公里判給波蘭。這個決定並非1919年停戰協議本身的一部分，而是在其後再次發生邊界衝突的背景下形成；1920年10月29日至11月6日的第二次戰鬥以及1921年的正式劃界，才固定兩國邊界的最終走向。就1919年的戰役本身而言，可靠結論是主戰線未被突破、戰鬥在米托停止，而領土爭議被延後，交由外交裁決與下一輪軍事對抗處理。
resultEn: The direct outcome of the 1919 campaign was the armistice signed at Mýto on 31 July, not the occupation of all Cieszyn Silesia by either army. At the ceasefire, Czechoslovakia held the larger southern industrial and railway zone, while Poland retained a northern area that included Cieszyn. The result was therefore a tactical stalemate and a strategic and diplomatic advantage for Czechoslovakia. On 28 August 1920, the Paris Conference of Ambassadors formally delimited the frontier, awarding 2,820.4 square kilometres to Czechoslovakia and 214.3 square kilometres, including Cieszyn, to Poland. That award was not part of the 1919 armistice itself; it followed amid renewed border fighting, and the Five-Day War of 29 October to 6 November 1920, followed by the 1921 demarcation, fixed the final course of the boundary. For the 1919 war itself, the established conclusion is that neither main front was broken, the fighting stopped at Mýto, and the territorial dispute was deferred to diplomatic adjudication and another round of military confrontation.
